newsitem.title: KUWAIT: United Arab Shipping sees '96 net fall to $70 mln.
newsitem.headline: United Arab Shipping sees '96 net fall to $70 mln.

text.p: The Arab world's largest shipping company, Kuwait-based United Arab Shipping (UASC), said on Tuesday it expects its net profit for 1996 to fall to $70 million from $87.1 million in 1995.
"UASC General Manager Abdulla al-Madi expected total net profits of the company in 1996 to be $70 million," the official Kuwait News Agency said in a report based on remarks by Madi.
In June UASC reported a 1995 net profit of $87.16 million after making a loss of $17.29 million in 1994.
"It (USAC) managed to make a net profit of $48 million until the end of August," the Agency reported Madi as saying. It did not explain the reason of the decline in profits.

The company plans to take delivery in 1998 of 10 new container ships worth $653.77 million being built for it by a consortium of Kawasaki Heavy Industries, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Company and Mitsui Engineering and Shipbuilding Company. The Shipbuilding project was announced in March.
UASC was formed in 1976 by the governments of Kuwait, Iraq, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar and Bahrain.
